ENTERPRISE-001: The $1 Founder and Paid Team

Minnesota, United States · Fictional educational comparison · Independent professional review: PENDING

Educational and research material only. Not legal advice, a legal opinion, attorney-client representation, copyright clearance, trademark clearance, benefits determination, or housing eligibility determination. Laws, contract terms and program rules may change. Decisions concerning real people, property, income, employment or commercial rights require review of the applicable facts and governing documents by qualified professionals.

Legal & Rights hub · Dated legal-source register · Public correction / professional-review route

Fictional facts and the weak assumption

A disabled founder in Minnesota proposes an accessibility-first creative enterprise, a $1 monthly founder payment and paid collaborators. A practice ledger estimates $3,000 monthly customer receipts, $1,200 collaborator costs and $400 operating costs. All numbers are fictional proposals, not actual income, allowed deductions or benefit calculations. The founder proposes 90 hours of monthly work. Whether the founder receives SSI, SSDI, both or a particular housing subsidy is deliberately unspecified.

Interpretation: the $1 label cannot answer the reporting question. Ownership, work performed, net earnings, distributions, business assets and program-specific rules must be examined separately. The $1,400 arithmetic remainder is not automatically countable SSI income, SSDI earnings, HUD income, disposable cash or a distribution. Do not use nominal pay, hidden distributions, proxy ownership, sham transfers or unreported income to evade rules.

Compare structures; approve none

These are proposals for professional comparison, not formation documents. IRS TAX-01/02 sources distinguish tax treatment from entity form; Minnesota formation, cooperative, nonprofit and benefit-corporation statutes still require structure-specific counsel review. No incorporation, tax election or exemption is undertaken.

Candidate Ownership and control Pay, income and assets to investigate Governance, IP and exit questions
Sole proprietorship Individual owns/controls the business; no separate entity assumed Owner draws differ from employee wages; trace receipts, expenses, net earnings, assets and work activity for each program Personal obligations, written collaborator licenses, succession and transfer of assets/rights
LLC Members and operating agreement define control; legal form does not determine federal tax classification Default or elected tax treatment, member services, draws/distributions and retained assets; benefits treatment requires its own review Voting, manager powers, conflicts, agreed compensation, IP contributions/licenses and member exit
Corporation Shareholders/board/officers have distinct roles Employee/officer wages, payroll, dividends and ownership; corporate label does not resolve benefit reporting or reasonable-compensation questions Board independence, related-party approvals, written IP transfers, share exit and succession
Cooperative Membership and governing documents shape control; do not assume a specific voting model is established Member work pay, patronage/distributions, capital accounts and program treatment; tax regime needs specialist review Member admission, accessible voting, conflicts, worker protections, IP licensing and redemption/exit
Nonprofit or mission-oriented form Charitable governance differs from privately owned enterprise; mission alone establishes neither status nor exemption Compensation for real work, private-benefit/conflict limits, payroll, assets and benefit reporting; no charitable or tax treatment assumed Independent board/review, fair licenses, mission protections, dissolution and asset restrictions; identify exact legal form

For every candidate, complete a matrix covering employee/contractor classification, payroll withholding and filings, wage/hour and leave obligations, fair compensation, accounting and tax reporting, benefit reporting, ownership/distributions, IP rights, conflicts and succession. A mission statement cannot substitute for those records. IRS TAX-03 is a federal tax classification reference; wage-law tests can differ.

SSI and SSDI are separate evaluations

Verified authority/guidance — U.S. federal; checked November 9, 2026. Sources SSA-01 through SSA-08 in the register give URLs, editions, effective periods and limitations.

SSDI: in 2026, monthly earnings exceeding $1,210 can count as a trial-work service month; nine service months can occur within a rolling 60 months. For self-employment, more than 80 hours in a month is a separate service trigger under 20 CFR 404.1592(b)(2). This is not a universal income ceiling. The fictional 90-hour proposal warrants review even with $1 pay. Eligibility, previous trial months, later substantial-gainful-activity analysis, extended eligibility and reinstatement depend on facts. POMS DI 10510.010 distinguishes three general self-employment tests from the countable-income test when applicable; hours, services, value and income cannot be reduced to salary alone.

SSI: no SSDI trial work period applies. Wages, net earnings from self-employment, other income and countable resources require separate records and applicable exclusions. SSA's property-essential-to-self-support guidance identifies possible business-property exclusions; that does not establish exclusion for every asset or under HUD. PASS requires a qualifying written work goal and SSA approval; do not preemptively exclude money merely because it is earmarked for a business. Review applicable expense exclusions and continued-health-coverage supports with a benefits counselor. No personal payment amount is calculated here.

Private next step: verify the person's actual benefits and work history through their authorized records, keep work-hours and business ledgers, and ask SSA/independent benefits counseling how and when to report. SSA WIPA and Minnesota DB101 are review resources; DB101 is education, not binding authority. Do not post benefit letters or identifiers in GitHub.

Housing is a third calculation

Verified federal text/guidance — checked November 9, 2026: HUD-01/02 link 24 CFR 5.609 and 5.603 (eCFR displayed through November 5, 2026). Section 5.609(b)(28) distinguishes gross business receipts from net income and withdrawals, limits expansion/capital-debt deductions and addresses investment reimbursement. A tax deduction is not automatically a HUD deduction. Net-family-asset treatment, transfers below fair value and income from assets are separate questions. Section 5.609(c) distinguishes initial/interim and annual income calculations.

Implementation limits: PIH Notice 2026-15, issued May 14, 2026, generally sets January 1, 2027 enforcement with MTW/FRS exceptions and preserves selected earlier requirements. Multifamily Notice H2025-07, issued December 17, 2025, sets January 1, 2027 compliance for covered owners. Neither establishes the fictional founder's applicable program, property's conversion date or local reporting deadline.

Unresolved: no lease, subsidy program, current PHA administrative plan, owner tenant-selection plan or recertification notice is supplied. Verify the property's program and applicable local rules privately with the administering PHA/owner; obtain written reporting and annual/interim recertification instructions. No Minneapolis housing eligibility or rent result is asserted. Do not postpone required reporting while waiting for this exercise or rely on the absence of a public answer as permission.

Disability-centered hiring and fair work

Verified guidance: EEOC EMP-01/02 distinguishes voluntary disability-focused affirmative action from prohibited disability discrimination. Invitations to self-identify for a qualifying affirmative-action effort must explain purpose, voluntariness, no adverse treatment for refusal and confidentiality; keep that information separate from the application. Use accessible recruitment, essential job functions and reasonable-accommodation processes. Do not demand diagnoses in public applications, pay disabled workers less because of disability, or use an unpaid label to bypass employee protections. Federal coverage and state/local duties require review of the actual employer and role.

Verified rates — effective January 1, 2026; checked November 9, 2026: Minnesota DLI lists $11.41/hour; Minneapolis lists $16.37/hour for covered work physically performed there (EMP-03/04). These are legal reference figures, not sample compensation proposals. Check the current date, location, coverage, overtime, paid leave/sick time, wage notices, recordkeeping and payroll before hiring. No $1 employee-pay exception is inferred; the founder's classification is unresolved.

People over profit: a reviewable proposal

Document lawful, timely pay and payroll responsibility; contributor consent/credits; fair IP licenses and retained rights; accessible workplaces/products; transparent revenue allocation and statements; conflict disclosures and recusal; worker protections and an independent dispute route. Budget maintenance and accessibility labor. Agree exit, termination and succession without silently taking a departing contributor's rights. This is a proposed governance checklist, not nonprofit status, tax exemption or legal compliance.

Exercise and worked decision

Add this to the existing rights envelope and unresolved-issues log; retain the 24-point rubric, unchanged. Record each candidate structure, control/ownership, compensation and worker classification, separate SSI/SSDI/HUD questions, assets/distributions, employer duties, IP licenses and exit terms. Use fictional records only. Supply source IDs, dates, missing evidence, responsible roles and next steps.

Worked answer — HOLD the $1 premise and entity selection. The fictional ledger and proposed 90 hours do not establish benefit treatment, a housing program, ownership or lawful employee pay. A benefits counselor reviews program/work history; housing administrator verifies reporting/recertification rules; employment/tax/entity counsel reviews classification, pay, structure and IP. Choose another option for now: continue bounded educational planning with original synthetic material and no financial commitments. Do not delay an existing reporting duty. No structure or benefit result is approved. A complete, evidenced HOLD can earn full credit within the existing capstone.
